gaggamo.meaning_2: name of a spirit (yakkha); rumbling sound; thunder
gaggamo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text gaggamo is a variant reading of gaggaro, a proper name in a list of yakkhas. Nominative singular.
gaggamo.example_1: 166. ‘‘ Ālambo gaggaro [gaggamo (syā.), bhaggaro (ka.)] bhīmo [bhimmo (ka.)], sādhuvādī ca saṃsayo;

bhimmo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for bhīmo in this list of names; one edition has bhimmo. Nominative singular.
bhimmo.example_1: 166. ‘‘ Ālambo gaggaro [gaggamo (syā.), bhaggaro (ka.)] bhīmo [bhimmo (ka.)], sādhuvādī ca saṃsayo;

kakkārikadāyikāvimānavatthu.meaning_2: story of the giver of kakkarikā (cucumber/gourd-plant); title of the fifteenth Vimānavatthu story
kakkārikadāyikāvimānavatthu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a Vimānavatthu story, treated here as an indeclinable title; the final member vatthu is neuter, but the whole title is undeclined in the text.

sujaka.meaning_2: name of a tree; Sujaka tree
sujaka.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading in the Vimānavatthu verse (Sī. syā. sujaka) for the tree-name in a list of trees; perhaps a species of tree or a shortened compound name. Appears in a compound (saḷalalabujabhujaka) in the text.
sujaka.translation_1: 650. “Adorned with Sal, Labuja, and Bhujaka trees, with flowering creepers hanging down;

paṇḍarīkasamonatā.meaning_2: abounding in white lotuses; covered with white water-lilies
paṇḍarīkasamonatā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of puṇḍarīkasamotatā at Vv 740; the sense is a lotus-filled pond. Nominative singular.
paṇḍarīkasamonatā.translation_1: Covered with various lotuses, filled with white water-lilies,

āḷambo.meaning_2: name of a drum; (a kind of) drum
āḷambo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a drum in a list of drums in Vimānavatthu verses. Nominative singular in the text. Related form āḷambara.
āḷambo.example_2: Āḷambo gaggaro bhīmo, sādhuvādī ca saṃsayo.
āḷambo.translation_2: Āḷamba, Gaggara, Bhīma, Sādhuvādī, and Saṃsaya,

abhipādayāmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular present. The text is addressed to the Buddha; often a sandhi/compound of abhi + pādayāmi gives this form, but here it is treated as one verb.
abhipādayāmi.example_1: Tayā hi bhante anukampito bhusaṃ, kataññutāya abhipādayāmi taṃ.
abhipādayāmi.translation_1: Indeed, venerable sir, I was intensely shown compassion by you, and out of gratitude, I pay homage to you.
